audit_findings.title: Acquisition growth may be valued without its required acquisition spending
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 1 percentage point of 2025 service-revenue growth; H1 2026 local-currency growth was 4% versus 3% organic; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth may include acquired revenue and earnings while acquisition payments are excluded from OE and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Service revenue benefited approximately 1% from acquisitions in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Acquisition contributions are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the 5% forecast assumes continuing acquisitions or how much recurring acquisition spending would be required. The mismatch is therefore possible rather than demonstrated, and its valuation materiality cannot be established from the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Separate historical and forecast organic growth from acquisition contributions, estimate normalized acquisition cash spending required for any acquisition-dependent growth, and rerun all scenarios using either organic growth or growth net of that spending.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $35.5 million, equal to $1.75 per diluted share and 0.34% of the $10,336 million bear equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid contingent consideration not captured in OE should reduce the equity bridge dollar-for-dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: The cumulative initial cash payments were $93.8 million and we may be required to pay additional consideration of up to $35.5 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge does not identify contingent consideration, so an omission is possible and the latest carrying liability requires reconciliation. Nevertheless, even the filed contractual maximum would reduce value by only $1.75 per share, which is too small to change the valuation conclusion. The company also paid $2.476 million and recognized $8.4 million of additional contingent-consideration expense in H1 2026, so the remaining claim must not be inferred solely from the original maximum.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 30, 2026 contingent-consideration carrying liability within accrued and other liabilities and other non-current liabilities, subtract amounts already paid or captured in OE, and deduct the remaining unpaid claim in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Plan-level pension deficits may not be offset by inaccessible surpluses elsewhere
audit_findings.magnitude: $103.0 million plan-level PBO deficit computed as $105.2 million obligation less $2.2 million assets; $5.08 per diluted share and 1.00% of bear equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An irrecoverable pension deficit belongs in the equity bridge; required contributions exceeding pension expense would also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The projected benefit obligation, the accumulated benefit obligation, and fair value of assets of these plans as of December 31, 2025 were $ 105.2 million, $ 95.6 million, and $ 2.2 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The underfunding of specific plans is demonstrated, while the inability to use surpluses from other plans remains unresolved. Even treating the full $103.0 million PBO deficit as an additional equity claim would reduce value by about $5.08 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. The expected $29.9 million of 2026 non-U.S. employer contributions may affect OE normalization but is also small relative to the $864.5 million anchor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest plan-by-plan funded status and legal surplus-recoverability analysis, trace the expected $29.9 million contributions against pension expense in OE, and rerun with only the irrecoverable deficit and contribution excess.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring tax-audit benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.5 million potential anchor overstatement; computed value impact approximately $232 million bear, $306 million base, and $361 million bull, or $11.45, $15.10, and $17.80 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time benefit retained in anchor OE is capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The reported tax rate in 2025 and 2024 includes a non-cash discrete current tax benefit of $13.7 million and $23.0 million, respectively, resulting from the reduction of uncertain tax position liabilities related to the settlement of a tax audit.
audit_findings.explanation: The $13.7 million current benefit and $5.8 million deferred benefit are demonstrably nonrecurring, but their retention in the $864.5 million anchor is not demonstrated. The cash-flow statement separately reverses the $13.685 million non-cash current benefit and includes deferred taxes as a reconciliation adjustment, so a cash-flow-derived OE calculation may already exclude them. Even if the full $19.5 million were retained, the computed reduction is about 2.3% of operating value and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace both tax benefits through the worksheet from 2025 net earnings to the $864.5 million anchor; if either survives the cash-flow adjustments, remove it and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Near-term capital requirements are above the latest-year run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.9 million forecast increase from $107.1 million in 2025 to approximately $130 million in 2026; sustaining portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance or mandatory capital expenditures reduce OE; growth capital should instead be matched to the growth it supports.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures in 2026 are expected to approximate $130 million subject to business and economic conditions and foreign currency fluctuations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $130 million amount is a forward-looking estimate, and H1 2026 actual capital expenditures were $45.2 million. The record does not establish whether the expected increase is recurring maintenance, mandatory systems spending, temporary timing, or growth investment. It is therefore not presently a demonstrated anchor error.
audit_findings.action: Compare full-year 2026 actual capital expenditures with the $130 million forecast, classify spending as maintenance, mandatory, or growth capital, and rerun OE if the recurring sustaining requirement exceeds $107.1 million.

audit_findings.title: Some foreign-earnings extraction taxes remain unprovided and unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring extraction taxes reduce distributable OE, while taxes required to access accumulated foreign cash or capital reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: All other undistributed earnings and any additional outside basis difference inherent in these entities and the contributed capital of our foreign subsidiaries are considered to be permanently reinvested on which no U.S. deferred income taxes or foreign withholding taxes have been provided.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that taxes have not been provided on some permanently reinvested earnings and outside-basis differences, but states that calculating the liability is impracticable. Non-U.S. operations generated $897.526 million, or 85.6% of 2025 pretax earnings, although that broad amount does not identify the earnings subject to unprovided extraction tax. The record therefore cannot establish whether the omitted tax is immaterial or reasonably capable of changing value.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction schedule of forecast earnings, accumulated distributable reserves, cash, existing repatriation-tax liabilities, legal remittance restrictions, and incremental withholding or other extraction taxes; then reduce OE or the bridge as appropriate and rerun the valuation.
